featured.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
featured.tldr: Penalizing reward hacking with a monitor during RL usually teaches the model to evade the monitor; this study shows which monitor designs resist evasion and which training choices reduce hacking.

featured.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
featured.tldr: PEARL trains a language model to recover from partly misaligned starts, making removal of a bad behavior far more resistant to later fine-tuning than standard supervised or reinforcement learning fixes.

featured.title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
featured.tldr: Training a chatbot to write an explicit, rule-checkable safety decision before it replies turns the shallowness of safety alignment into a defense against multi-turn jailbreaks, without a judge model in the reward.

featured.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
featured.tldr: Rubric rewards for open-ended RL only measure coverage, so models learn to pad; adding a precision term for necessary, factually correct sentences raises win rate over the base model from 10.6% to 68.0%.

featured.title: Thinking-in-Bets at Test Time Reduces Sycophantic Revisions in LLM Agents
featured.tldr: Having an agent privately record its claims, evidence and confidence before reading user feedback sharply cuts sycophantic reversals of correct work while still letting it fix real bugs, without any training.
